title: Projection-compatible sheafification of positive affine module quotients
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J$ ideal sheaf data, $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $I=J(X)$, and $L$ tilde followed by pullback along the canonical affine isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections, def-pc-module-pullback]. For every $A$-module $M$ and integer $n>0$, there is an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{formalModuleQuotient}(J,n,L(M))\cong L(M/I^nM)$, for the explicit quotient of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], such that the sheaf quotient projection followed by $e$ is $L$ of the module quotient projection. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 087W, positive affine quotient systems; Schemes Tags 01I7, 01IC (exact affine correspondence) and 01I8 (tensor comparison)

proof.text: On Spec A, apply the affine projection theorem. Its surjection with kernel I^n M induces a linear quotient equivalence. Positive ideal powers are quasi-coherent; multiplication has quasi-coherent image and cokernel by tensor, kernel and cokernel closure. The affine counit therefore turns the section equivalence into a sheaf isomorphism. Cancel its image of the module quotient isomorphism and use counit naturality and the left adjunction triangle to prove the projection equation.

The ideal-power pullback image equality identifies the pulled-back product image with the product by the extended power. Tensor pullback is a left adjoint and preserves cokernels. Compose cokernel.mapIso, cokernelImageι and the preservation comparison to obtain a quotient isomorphism whose projection is the pulled-back projection.

Transport along X isoSpec: the ideal on Spec A is J comap isoSpec.inv and its top ideal is I mapped through ΓSpecIso.inv. The affine ideal extension formula and toSpecΓ_appTop prove this identity; comap_comp and the inverse identities recover J. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives tensorPullback isomorphic to Mathlib pullback. Map this isomorphism through the explicit quotient functor and compose the two preceding comparisons. Cokernel projection equations and naturality of the pullback comparison prove the required projection identity.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_formalQuotient_comparison
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    let A := Γ(X, ⊤)
    let I := J.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩
    let L := tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom
    ∃ e : formalModuleQuotient J n (L.obj M) ≅
        L.obj (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)))),
      formalModuleQuotientπ J n (L.obj M) ≫ e.hom =
        L.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)).mkQ)
